blocks.text: This connects back to recapping quantization, already covered in this topic. QLoRA genuinely quantizes the frozen, pretrained base model down to a genuinely low bit precision.

Since those genuinely base weights already stay frozen, already covered in LoRA, reduced precision genuinely costs little accuracy, a genuinely clever pairing explored throughout the rest of this topic.

10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates quantizing a frozen base weight while keeping a small LoRA matrix pair at higher precision, both already covered in this topic.

code.content:
def quantize_4bit(value, scale=0.1):
    # already covered as quantizing the frozen base model in this topic
    quantized_int = round(value / scale)
    return quantized_int, quantized_int * scale  # returns (stored int, dequantized approximation)

# already covered as the frozen base model in this topic
base_weight = 0.734
quantized_int, dequantized_weight = quantize_4bit(base_weight)
print(f"Original base weight (already covered in this topic): {base_weight}")
print(f"Quantized representation (already covered in this topic): {quantized_int}")
print(f"Dequantized for computation (already covered as computation during training in this topic): {dequantized_weight}")

# already covered as LoRA matrices staying at higher precision in this topic
lora_a = 0.10234567  # genuinely kept at full precision, unlike the base weight above
lora_b = -0.20456789
lora_update = lora_a * lora_b

merged_weight = dequantized_weight + lora_update
print(f"\nLoRA update, kept at full precision (already covered in this topic): {lora_update:.6f}")
print(f"Final merged weight at inference time: {merged_weight:.6f}")

blocks.text: 11. Fine-Tuning LLMs: Progress Recap

items: QLoRA extends LoRA with quantization, combining two efficiency techniques into one approach.
It quantizes the frozen, pretrained base model down to a low bit precision.
The small, trainable LoRA matrices stay at higher precision, since they are the ones actually trained.
LoRA's small parameter count and quantization's memory reduction stack together for a bigger combined saving.
This combined reduction makes fine-tuning very large models possible on modest, single-GPU hardware.
During each forward pass, quantized weights get temporarily dequantized, trading compute for memory savings.
QLoRA suits large models on limited hardware; plain LoRA suffices when memory is not the binding constraint.
Next up: Prefix Tuning, another parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach with a different mechanism.
